Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling a smaller version of itself. To work correctly, it must include a "base case," which is a condition that tells the function when to stop. A common way to visualize this is opening Russian nesting dolls, where you keep uncovering smaller dolls until you reach the final, solid one.
